commands.short: Build, test, and publish Caplo agents and tool packages, and manage workspaces, remote MCP servers, secrets, and customer identity keys
commands.long:
caplo builds, tests, and publishes Caplo agents and tool packages from a project folder, and manages a
workspace's agents, tool packages, remote MCP servers, secrets, knowledge bases, channels, API clients,
customer identity keys, and subscription billing.

A person logs in with caplo auth login. CI and automation set CAPLO_API_KEY to an API client's key and
CAPLO_WORKSPACE to its workspace ID instead; see caplo workspace api-client. Commands act on the workspace that
--workspace or CAPLO_WORKSPACE names, else the one selected with caplo workspace use.

The configuration directory is CAPLO_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.config/caplo ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/caplo), or %AppData%\caplo
on Windows. It holds config.yaml: the API URL, issuer, OAuth client, credential storage, and selected workspace.
Use a separate CAPLO_CONFIG_DIR for each Caplo installation you log in to.

Exit codes: 0 for success, 1 for an error, 2 for a usage error (including a confirmation that needs --yes when
there is no terminal), 3 when a check fails (validation, tool fixtures, eval cases, or assertion checks), 130 when
Ctrl-C interrupts a command or a prompt, and 143 for SIGTERM. A second Ctrl-C ends the process at once.
commands.example:
caplo auth login
  caplo init shop --template summit
  caplo publish --env prod --yes

commands.short: Chat with the agent's saved draft, or a release, in a private test conversation
commands.long:
Starts a private test conversation with the agent's saved draft, or with a release named by --release, and reads
one message per line from standard input. Each reply is printed with the sub-agents and tools the turn used. End
with Ctrl-D, /exit, or /quit; the test session is closed when the chat ends.

A write awaiting a decision is shown as its review, as a review of the whole plan, or as a write that can only be
declined: one with no review here, or one waiting for the customer to sign in. /confirm or /cancel decides the write
shown last, as the widget's buttons do; ordinary text never approves a write. If the write changed meanwhile, the
current one is shown to answer again, and a refused (409) message or decision is reported without ending the chat.
A message or decision that was not sent makes the command exit 1 at its end; without a terminal, a failed turn
makes it exit 3.

Replies arrive on the agent-test event stream. It resumes after the last event when it reconnects, reloads the
history on a reset, reconnects with a fresh token when asked to reauthenticate, and retries network failures, 429,
and 5xx, but not an unknown host, a rejected TLS certificate, or another 4xx. When no test session is free, caplo
agent test list and caplo agent test close free one.
commands.example:
caplo agent chat "Shop Concierge"
  caplo agent chat "Shop Concierge" --release 2.1.0
  printf 'Where is order 1042?\n/confirm\n' | caplo agent chat "Shop Concierge"

commands.short: Pin tools, run the evals, and publish the agent's saved draft as a release
commands.long:
Publishes the saved draft of a workspace agent: it pins the draft's tool versions, checks that the draft is
ready, runs its eval cases, and publishes it. The agent needs at least one eval case, and every case must pass. Its
sub-agents must have releases already; caplo publish releases a project's agents together.

A released draft is published again only when its packages have newer versions. When its eval cases changed since
its release, they run against it and the release is kept.

Without --bump the version follows the console: a first release, or a change of sub-agents, provider, or model, or
a removed tool, action, or knowledge base, is major; an added one is minor; anything else is a patch. It asks before
publishing; --yes skips the question.
commands.example:
caplo agent publish "Shop Concierge"
  caplo agent publish "Shop Concierge" --bump minor --yes

commands.short: Log in through the browser, or with --device on a machine without one
commands.long:
Logs in with the caplo-cli OpenID client: in the browser with the authorization code flow and PKCE, answered on
a 127.0.0.1 port, or with --device through the device authorization grant. The refresh token is stored in the OS
keychain, or with --insecure-storage (or credential-storage file) in a 0600 file in the configuration directory;
access tokens stay in memory. Refresh tokens rotate on every use, and caplo processes share a lock so that none
reuses a token another has used.

The API and issuer are --api-url and --issuer, else CAPLO_API_URL and CAPLO_ISSUER, else the saved settings, else
production (https://api.caplo.si and https://auth.caplo.si/realms/caplo). A successful login saves them, so the
variables affect login only and never redirect an existing session. Login keeps the selected workspace while you
still belong to it, and otherwise selects your only workspace.
commands.example:
caplo auth login
  caplo auth login --device
  caplo auth login --api-url https://api.staging.example.com --issuer https://auth.staging.example.com/realms/caplo

commands.short: List channels and deploy agent releases to them
commands.long:
A channel is a website widget, WhatsApp number, Messenger or Instagram account, Outlook mailbox, or phone number,
and serves one agent release. Channels are created in the console; deploy and rollback change the release they serve.
New conversations get the new release, and open ones keep the release they started with. A channel is named by its
ID, its name, or <kind>/<name>. Every other setting of a channel stays as it is, and its revision guards a deploy
against a concurrent change in the console.

commands.short: Create a project: caplo.yaml, agent files, and tool packages
commands.long:
Creates a project in dir (default: the current directory), which must be missing or empty. The blank
template has one agent; summit is a sample shop with a concierge agent, three sub-agents, and two tool packages.
Each tool package gets package.json and tsconfig.json from the @caplo/tools templates; run npm install in it
before testing it.

A project is a folder with caplo.yaml: apiVersion v1, kind Project, a name, and the agents and tools globs
(default agents/*.yaml and tools/*). Project commands find it by walking up from the current directory or --dir.
Each agent file is an agent YAML document with apiVersion v2.0.0, the format of the console's Export YAML; v1
files are refused. The file name without .yaml is the agent's key, which links and selectors use. Each tool
package is a directory with its own caplo.yaml, as caplo tool init makes it.

In an agent file:

  subAgents link a project agent with local: <file key>, or any workspace agent with agentId. With release:
  latest, or no release, the link pins the child's newest release that is not revoked whenever the parent is
  pushed or published, so a child's new release publishes its parents again. A version pins that release. The
  child runs with its own release's tools and knowledge.

  tools name <package>/<tool> for a project package, <server>/<tool> for a published tool of a workspace remote
  MCP server (caplo mcp), or <package ID>/<tool>; a package alone selects all its tools. A name that is no
  project package is looked up as a remote MCP server when the project is diffed, pushed, or published.

  knowledgeBases name a workspace knowledge base by name or ID. A name resolves in the workspace the command acts
  on, so one file works in every environment.

  evals are the agent's eval cases; see caplo eval.

Workspace agents and packages are matched by name: a missing one is created and an existing one updated. Nothing
is deleted; caplo publish --prune archives agents the project no longer defines.
commands.example:
caplo init shop --template summit
  cd shop && (cd tools/order-desk && npm install) && (cd tools/store-stock && npm install)
  caplo init --name support

commands.short: Manage knowledge bases and their files, and search them
commands.long:
A knowledge base holds files an agent answers from. An uploaded file is published: it is read, cut into passages
and indexed, and then goes live by itself, so from the next question on every agent using the knowledge base can find
it. Unpublishing a file takes it out of agents' answers at once and keeps it stored and indexed, so publishing it again
is instant. Replacing a file keeps its old content answering until the new content is live; if the new content cannot
be read, the old content stays live and the file says why. Deleting a file removes it from search at once. Agent files
name knowledge bases by name or ID, and so do these commands.

When the knowledge service refuses a change, such as deleting a knowledge base agents use or going over one of the
workspace's limits, the command prints the service's sentence saying what to do and exits 1.
commands.example:
caplo knowledge create "Returns policy" --description "Return and refund rules"
  caplo knowledge files upload "Returns policy" ./refunds.pdf --wait
  caplo knowledge search "Returns policy" "How long do I have to return a jacket?"

stay, and it prints the refusal and how many files were not uploaded. Any other refusal, such as a file whose

deletes nothing and exits 1, saying how many files were refused.

commands.short: Validate, push, test, evaluate, and publish bottom up: tools, then child agents, then parents
commands.long:
Publishes the selection, or the whole project, bottom up. Changed packages are pushed, built, tested with their
fixtures on the workspace's test runner, and published first. Then agents publish with children before parents:
each draft is saved pinned to its children's new releases, its eval cases run, and it is published. An agent
publishes when its file changed, its saved draft is unpublished, or a package or release: latest sub-agent it uses
publishes. A release does not pin eval cases, so an agent whose cases alone changed since its release is evaluated
and keeps the release. A published agent needs at least one eval case, and every case must pass.

It validates the project, prints the plan and diffs, and asks before publishing; --yes skips the question. Without
a terminal, and on a project's first publish to a workspace, it needs --yes. --dry-run prints the plan only.
--prune archives the agents an earlier publish of this project created that it no longer defines; it takes no
selectors.

Selectors are agent/<file key or name>, where a file key wins over a name, and tool/<package>. An agent brings
its project sub-agents and the project packages they use. Without selectors the command acts on the whole project.

Selecting an agent also selects the project agents that link it at release: latest, since its new release
publishes them again.

Environments. caplo.yaml may define environments, each a workspace the project publishes to:

  environments:
    staging:
      workspace: 5b1e9c2a-...        # an ID, or a name when you log in rather than use an API key
      apiKeyEnv: CAPLO_STAGING_KEY   # optional: the variable with this environment's API key
    prod:
      workspace: 0d6a3c87-...
      apiKeyEnv: CAPLO_PROD_KEY
      promoteFrom: staging           # publish only what staging released from the same source
      agents:                        # agent fields by file key, merged over the agent file
        front: {model: {name: claude-sonnet-4-5}}
      channels:                      # channels a publish points at the agent's newest release
        front: [Website, twilio/Support line]

--env, or CAPLO_ENV, selects one for validate, diff, push, eval, and publish: its workspace (a different
--workspace or CAPLO_WORKSPACE is refused), its API key when its apiKeyEnv variable is set (used instead of
CAPLO_API_KEY), and its agent fields, which merge like a JSON merge patch: mappings merge, null removes a key, and
anything else replaces.

Each release's note names the project and the agent's source digest: its file as written, the files of the project
packages it uses, and its project sub-agents. With promoteFrom, the publish exits 3 unless every agent it publishes
has a release in that environment, not revoked, with the same digest. That environment is read with its own
apiKeyEnv key, else the login session; a publish that uses an API key needs the other environment's key, with
agents:read. After publishing, it deploys the environment's channels that do not serve their agent's newest
release, which needs channels:write; the plan lists them as channel/<kind>/<name>.

With -o json or yaml the plan is one document: the project, workspace, environment, whether anything changes,
and per resource its steps (create, update, save-evals, build, test, evaluate, publish, archive, deploy; none when
unchanged), summary, changed files, reasons, current and next versions, and diff. A pipeline can post it on a pull
request or check it with a policy. push and publish print it only with --dry-run.
commands.example:
caplo publish
  caplo publish agent/orders --dry-run
  caplo publish --env prod --yes
  caplo publish --prune

runner. It exits 3 when a fixture fails.

commands.long:
Checks the project without calling the workspace: caplo.yaml and each package's caplo.yaml, every agent file
against the agent schema, unique agent names and file keys, references to project agents and packages, the tools an
mcp package declares, sub-agent link cycles, and each agent's depth limit: at most policy.maxDepth (1 to 4, default
3) sub-agent links below it. Tools of remote MCP servers are checked when the project is diffed, pushed, or
published.

An agent with routing mode fast needs at least one sub-agent and doNotUseWhen on every link. When its file lists
evals, each sub-agent also needs two cases that set routedBy and name it in subAgent.

Every environment in caplo.yaml is checked: the agent keys it names and its agent fields merged over each file.
With --env, the agents are checked as that environment publishes them. Problems are printed and the command
exits 3.

commands.short: Manage API clients and their keys for CI and automation
commands.long:
An API client authenticates CI and automation without a person's login. Set CAPLO_API_KEY to one of its keys and
CAPLO_WORKSPACE (or --workspace, or a project environment's workspace) to its workspace ID, and caplo commands act as
the client with its scopes, at CAPLO_API_URL, else the configured API, else production. caplo auth status shows the
client and its scopes. A key cannot list workspaces, so a workspace named by name is refused.

Scopes:
  agents:read, agents:write, agents:publish
  tools:read, tools:write, tools:publish
  channels:read, channels:write
  conversations:read, usage:read
  endpoints:read, endpoints:write

A write or publish scope includes its read scope, and a member can grant only the actions their own role holds.
A CI publish needs agents:write and agents:publish, and tools:write and
tools:publish when the project has packages. An environment that deploys channels needs channels:write, which a
publish checks before it starts. Channel commands also read agents, and knowledge commands use the agent scopes.

A project environment can name its own key variable with apiKeyEnv; see caplo publish.
commands.example:
caplo workspace api-client create ci --scope agents:write,agents:publish,tools:write,tools:publish
  CAPLO_API_KEY=... CAPLO_WORKSPACE=5b1e9c2a-... caplo publish --yes
